content.value_statement: Organizations struggle to convert specialist data knowledge into reliable agent systems. This skill provides structured methods for requirements, capabilities, workflows, controls, and evaluation.
actual_capabilities: Prioritizes platform requirements across six data asset management modules.
Structures expert knowledge into searchable entries, rules, and delivery templates.
Defines agent capabilities and boundaries across a six-layer model.
Designs workflows with explicit human review and intervention points.
Plans security, compliance, audit trails, and evidence mechanisms.
Defines operating metrics for time, cost, capacity, and review quality.
limitations: Provides designs and document drafts, not deployed software or infrastructure.
Does not replace licensed legal, valuation, security, or regulatory professionals.
Cost and schedule ranges require validation against local scope and resources.
Policy references and platform knowledge may require updates before use.

use_cases.title: Plan a Data Agent Platform
use_cases.description: Create prioritized requirements, modules, delivery phases, and governance controls for a new platform.

use_cases.title: Structure Expert Knowledge
use_cases.description: Convert specialist documents into searchable knowledge entries, decision rules, and reusable templates.

use_cases.title: Review Agent Controls
use_cases.description: Define capability boundaries, human checkpoints, security requirements, audit evidence, and operating metrics.

prompt_templates.title: Identify Platform Requirements
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [business goal] and [user needs]. List platform requirements, priorities, assumptions, and required human decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Structure a Knowledge Collection
prompt_templates.prompt: Transform [document set] into knowledge entries, rules, templates, metadata, and an update process. Flag missing evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Agent Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a workflow for [task]. Define inputs, reasoning stages, tool calls, outputs, controls, and human intervention points.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Platform Delivery Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a phased plan for [platform]. Cover architecture, integrations, security, compliance, evidence, testing, operations, metrics, dependencies, and risks.

output_examples.input: Design requirements for a data inventory agent used by enterprise data teams.
output: Priority: inventory ingestion, classification, quality checks, and review queues.
Human checkpoint: approve classifications and exceptions before publication.
Controls: authorization, data isolation, audit logs, and versioned rules.
Metrics: review acceptance, completion time, exception rate, and cost per inventory.

output_examples.input: Plan how to convert expert documents into an agent knowledge base.
output: Separate policy facts, decision rules, procedures, templates, and examples.
Attach source, owner, effective date, jurisdiction, and review status.
Test retrieval coverage and require evidence citations in generated drafts.

output_examples.input: Define boundaries for an automated data asset assessment workflow.
output_examples.output: The agent may prepare evidence summaries and draft assessments. Qualified reviewers must approve valuations, legal conclusions, and final customer deliverables.

best_practices: Provide business goals, target users, source documents, constraints, and required deliverables.
Verify every policy, cost, schedule, and compliance claim against current authoritative sources.
Keep human approval points for regulated decisions, exceptions, and final deliverables.
anti_patterns: Do not treat generated drafts as legal, valuation, or regulatory opinions.
Do not automate workflows before defining permissions, evidence, boundaries, and review ownership.
Do not estimate platform cost or duration without scope, integration, security, and staffing details.

faq.question: What does this skill design?
faq.answer: It designs requirements, knowledge structures, agent capabilities, workflows, controls, evidence mechanisms, operations, and evaluation plans.

faq.question: Does it build a working platform?
faq.answer: No. It produces designs, plans, checklists, and document drafts for implementation teams.

faq.question: Can it replace data specialists?
faq.answer: No. It supports repeatable analysis and drafting while qualified people retain judgment, approval, and accountability.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide goals, users, current processes, source documents, systems, constraints, regulations, risks, and expected outputs.

faq.question: How does it address security?
faq.answer: It prompts for authorization, isolation, encryption, auditability, compliance assessment, evidence retention, and human review.

faq.question: Can it estimate costs and schedules?
faq.answer: It can provide planning ranges, but teams must validate them against scope, architecture, suppliers, staffing, and local requirements.
